revealWordProblem.title: Apply: School District Size
revealWordProblem.text: A large school district has 621,000 students in grades kindergarten through 12. The district currently has 1 teacher for every 20 students but plans to hire more teachers to have 1 teacher for every 15 students. How many teachers does the school district need to hire to reach its goal?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The district hires 10,350 teachers. It currently has 621,000 ÷ 20 = 31,050 teachers, and it needs 621,000 ÷ 15 = 41,400 teachers to reach the new ratio. The difference is 41,400 − 31,050 = 10,350 teachers to hire.

turnAndTalk.question: The station must divide 1,344 nutrition bars equally among 12 crew sections. Before dividing, about how many bars should each section get, and how do you know?

turnAndTalk.question: In a division problem, what is the difference between the quotient and the remainder, and what does each one tell you?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The quotient is the size of each equal share; the remainder is what is left over.

stems.en: The quotient tells me ___, and the remainder tells me ___.
stems.es: El cociente me dice ___, y el residuo me dice ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students explain the quotient is the number in each group while the remainder is the amount left that cannot be shared equally, and a remainder of 0 means it divides evenly.
turnAndTalk.extend: When is it correct to round a quotient UP because of a remainder, and when should you drop the remainder? Give an example of each.

turnAndTalk.kernel: Repeat the cycle Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down until no digits are left to bring down; what is left at the end is the remainder.

visual.title: 1,344 ÷ 12, one place at a time
visual.caption: Long division writes one quotient digit per place: 1, 1, 2 — so each of the 12 sections gets 112 bars

conceptIntro.heading: How do you divide big numbers?
conceptIntro.intro: Dividing means splitting a total into equal groups. Long division finds the quotient one digit at a time by repeating the same four steps: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Repeat the cycle Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down until no digits are left to bring down; what is left at the end is the remainder.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want 1,344 ÷ 12. The dividend is 1,344 and the divisor is 12, so 12 goes outside the bracket and 1,344 goes inside.
DIVIDE: 12 does not fit into 1, so I look at 13. How many 12s fit into 13? One. I write 1 above the 3.
SUBTRACT: 13 − 12 = 1. That is what is left so far.
BRING DOWN: I bring the next digit, 4, down next to the 1 to make 14. Now I repeat the cycle.
REPEAT: 14 ÷ 12 → 1 (written above the 4), 1 × 12 = 12, 14 − 12 = 2, and I bring down the last 4 to make 24.
REPEAT: 24 ÷ 12 → 2 (written above the last 4), 2 × 12 = 24, 24 − 24 = 0. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 0.
The digits I wrote are 1, 1, 2, so 1,344 ÷ 12 = 112. I check by multiplying: 12 × 112 = 1,344.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's do 384 ÷ 8. DIVIDE: 8 does not fit into 3, so we look at 38. How many 8s fit into 38? (4 — write it above the 8.)
MULTIPLY: 4 × 8 = ? (32 — write it under the 38.) SUBTRACT: 38 − 32 = ? (6.)
BRING DOWN: bring the 4 down to make 64, then repeat. DIVIDE: 64 ÷ 8 = ? (8.) MULTIPLY: 8 × 8 = 64. SUBTRACT: 64 − 64 = 0.
Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 0 and 384 ÷ 8 = 48. Check: 8 × 48 = 384.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next, you will sort the steps of the long division for 1,344 ÷ 12 and then divide on your own.
Remember the cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — and repeat until no digits are left.

explore.instructions: Divide 1,344 ÷ 12 with long division. Sort each card — is it a step in the divide, multiply, subtract, bring down cycle for this problem, or is it NOT a step in this division?

items.text: DIVIDE: 12 fits into 13 one time, so write 1 above the 3.
BRING DOWN: bring the next 4 down to make 14.
REPEAT: 24 ÷ 12 → 2, then 24 − 24 = 0, so the remainder is 0.
Add the dividend and the divisor: 1,344 + 12 = 1,356.
Bring down two digits at once to make 134.
Write the leftover 1 into the quotient instead of above the bar.

discourse.prompt: How does the divide, multiply, subtract, bring down cycle help you divide 1,344 by 12? What is 1,344 ÷ 12?
discourse.sentenceFrame: 1,344 ÷ 12 = ___ because I repeated divide, multiply, subtract, and bring down until no digits were left, and the leftover at the end was ___.

choiceFeedback: 48 × 12 is only 576 — this answer is missing a whole place value. The quotient needs three digits; estimate 12 × 400 = 4,800 to see the right size.
The digits look familiar, but the place value is off: 12 × 480 = 5,760. Check where each digit of your quotient lands.
12 × 380 = 4,560, which misses 4,896. Recheck the very first step: how many 12s fit into 48?
hints: Division asks how many groups of 12 fit inside 4,896, so the answer should be in the hundreds, not the tens.
Work through the long division one place value at a time, and remember to write a 0 in the quotient whenever the divisor does not fit.
Start with 48 ÷ 12 = 4, so the hundreds digit is 4. Now bring down the 9 — how many 12s fit into 9? Decide that digit and keep going.
hintsEs: La división pregunta cuántos grupos de 12 caben dentro de 4,896, así que la respuesta debe estar en las centenas, no en las decenas.
Haz la división larga un valor posicional a la vez, y recuerda escribir un 0 en el cociente cuando el divisor no quepa.
Empieza con 48 ÷ 12 = 4, así que el dígito de las centenas es 4. Ahora baja el 9: ¿cuántos 12 caben en 9? Decide ese dígito y continúa.

choiceFeedback: 29 × 25 = 725, only one-tenth of 7,225 — a zero got dropped. Estimate first: 25 × 300 = 7,500, so the quotient must be in the hundreds.
That is ten times too large: 25 × 2,890 = 72,250. Count the place values in your quotient.
25 × 389 = 9,725, which overshoots 7,225. Recheck the tens digit after you take out the first 200 groups of 25.
hints: Think in 25s: this asks how many groups of 25 make up 7,225, and that count will be in the hundreds.
Set it up as long division and start the cycle: how many 25s fit into 72?
DIVIDE: 72 ÷ 25 → 2. MULTIPLY: 2 × 25 = 50. SUBTRACT: 72 − 50 = 22. BRING DOWN the 2 to make 222, then repeat the cycle.
hintsEs: Piensa en grupos de 25: esto pregunta cuántos grupos de 25 forman 7,225, y esa cantidad estará en las centenas.
Escríbelo como división larga y empieza el ciclo: ¿cuántos 25 caben en 72?
DIVIDE: 72 ÷ 25 → 2. MULTIPLICA: 2 × 25 = 50. RESTA: 72 − 50 = 22. BAJA el 2 para formar 222 y repite el ciclo.

optional.stem: A school orders 3,648 pencils packed 24 to a box. How many boxes are there?
choiceFeedback: 148 × 24 = 3,552, which leaves 96 pencils with no box. Multiply your quotient by 24 and check that it gives back exactly 3,648.
24 × 160 = 3,840, more pencils than the school ordered. Trim the tens digit and multiply back to test it.
24 × 144 = 3,456, which leaves 192 pencils with no box. Those still need boxes, so the quotient is not finished.
optional.stemEs: Una escuela pide 3,648 lápices empacados de 24 por caja. ¿Cuántas cajas hay?
hints: Every box holds the same number of pencils, so this is asking how many equal groups of 24 fit into 3,648.
Set it up as long division and DIVIDE first — how many 24s fit into 36?
DIVIDE: 36 ÷ 24 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 24 = 24. SUBTRACT: 36 − 24 = 12. BRING DOWN the 4 to make 124, then repeat the cycle.
hintsEs: Cada caja tiene la misma cantidad de lápices, así que esto pregunta cuántos grupos iguales de 24 caben en 3,648.
Escríbelo como división larga y DIVIDE primero: ¿cuántos 24 caben en 36?
DIVIDE: 36 ÷ 24 → 1. MULTIPLICA: 1 × 24 = 24. RESTA: 36 − 24 = 12. BAJA el 4 para formar 124 y repite el ciclo.

optional.explanation: 31 × 164 = 5,084 exactly, so there is no remainder.
choiceFeedback: 154 × 31 = 4,774, which leaves 310 — enough for 10 more groups of 31, so the tens digit is off. Recheck the tens place of your quotient.
31 × 174 = 5,394, which is past 5,084. Your estimate for the tens digit is one too high — multiply back to test it.
Your quotient is doing the right work, but check the leftover. Multiply the quotient by 31 and subtract from 5,084 to see whether anything actually remains.
optional.explanationEs: 31 × 164 = 5,084 exactamente, así que no hay residuo.
hints: You are finding how many groups of 31 fit inside 5,084 — and whether anything is left over at the end.
Estimate first: 31 is close to 30, and 5,084 ÷ 30 is a little under 170. Then divide exactly.
DIVIDE: 31 does not fit into 5, so start with 50. 50 ÷ 31 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 31 = 31. SUBTRACT: 50 − 31 = 19. BRING DOWN the 8 and repeat, watching the very last leftover.
hintsEs: Estás buscando cuántos grupos de 31 caben dentro de 5,084, y si sobra algo al final.
Estima primero: 31 está cerca de 30, y 5,084 ÷ 30 es un poco menos de 170. Luego divide con exactitud.
DIVIDE: el 31 no cabe en 5, así que empieza con 50. 50 ÷ 31 → 1. MULTIPLICA: 1 × 31 = 31. RESTA: 50 − 31 = 19. BAJA el 8 y repite, atento a lo que sobra al final.

optional.stem: Path 1: The first arcade door shows 4,928 ÷ 7. Which quotient lights the correct path?
optional.explanation: 7 × 704 = 4,928 exactly, so the quotient is 704 with no remainder.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 7 × 704 = 4,928 exactly, so the quotient is 704 with no remainder.
The digits are close, but 7 × 740 = 5,180. Check where the 0 belongs in the quotient — its position changes the value a lot.
A remainder can never be as large as the divisor. If your leftover is 7 or more, another whole group of 7 still fits, so keep dividing.
optional.stemEs: Camino 1: La primera puerta del arcade muestra 4,928 ÷ 7. ¿Cuál cociente ilumina el camino correcto?
optional.explanationEs: 7 × 704 = 4,928 exactamente, así que el cociente es 704 sin residuo.
hints: Behind the arcade story this is plain division: how many groups of 7 are inside 4,928?
Divide place by place, and write a 0 in the quotient at any spot where 7 does not fit.
49 ÷ 7 = 7, so the hundreds digit is 7. Next you look at 2 — does 7 fit into 2? Record that digit and keep going.
hintsEs: Detrás de la historia del arcade esto es una división normal: ¿cuántos grupos de 7 hay dentro de 4,928?
Divide valor posicional por valor posicional, y escribe un 0 en el cociente en cualquier lugar donde el 7 no quepa.
49 ÷ 7 = 7, así que el dígito de las centenas es 7. Después miras el 2: ¿cabe el 7 en 2? Anota ese dígito y continúa.

optional.stem: Path 2: A side corridor displays 6,045 ÷ 9. Which door is correct?
choiceFeedback: 671 × 9 = 6,039, which is 6 short of 6,045 — that leftover 6 is a remainder. Don't drop the remainder when the division doesn't come out even.
Check by multiplying: 9 × 672 = 6,048, which is already more than 6,045, so this quotient is too big before any remainder is added.
Your remainder makes sense, but a digit went missing from the quotient. Count place values — 6,045 reaches the thousands, so the quotient reaches the hundreds.
optional.stemEs: Camino 2: Un pasillo lateral muestra 6,045 ÷ 9. ¿Cuál puerta es la correcta?
hints: The divisor does not have to fit evenly here, so your answer may include a remainder.
Divide one place value at a time and keep careful track of what is left after the very last step.
60 ÷ 9 = 6 with 6 left over, so 6 goes in the hundreds place. Bring down the 4 to make 64 and keep going, watching the final leftover.
hintsEs: Aquí el divisor no tiene que caber exactamente, así que tu respuesta puede incluir un residuo.
Divide un valor posicional a la vez y lleva bien la cuenta de lo que queda después del último paso.
60 ÷ 9 = 6 y sobran 6, así que el 6 va en las centenas. Baja el 4 para formar 64 y continúa, atento a lo que sobra al final.

optional.instructions: Path 3: Each door shows a finished long-division result. Sort them — does the arcade door light up CORRECT, or is the quotient WRONG?
optional.explanation: Multiplying each quotient by its divisor tells you which doors light up: 12 × 438 = 5,256, 14 × 585 = 8,190, and 23 × 129 = 2,967 all rebuild their dividends, so those are correct. The other three fail the check — 12 × 619 = 7,428 not 7,308, 15 × 275 = 4,125 not 4,275, and 16 × 34 = 544, which is ten times too small for 5,440.
optional.explanationEs: Multiplicar cada cociente por su divisor te dice qué puertas se encienden: 12 × 438 = 5,256, 14 × 585 = 8,190 y 23 × 129 = 2,967 reconstruyen sus dividendos, así que esos son correctos. Los otros tres no pasan la prueba: 12 × 619 = 7,428 y no 7,308, 15 × 275 = 4,125 y no 4,275, y 16 × 34 = 544, que es diez veces menor que 5,440.
hints: A quotient is only correct if the divisor times the quotient rebuilds the dividend exactly — no card here has a remainder to worry about.
Instead of re-dividing every door, multiply the quotient shown on the card by the divisor and compare it to the dividend.
Start with 5,440 ÷ 16 = 34: multiply 16 × 34 and compare the product to 5,440. That size check alone tells you which pile that door belongs in.
hintsEs: Un cociente solo es correcto si el divisor por el cociente reconstruye el dividendo exactamente; aquí ninguna tarjeta tiene residuo.
En vez de volver a dividir cada puerta, multiplica el cociente que muestra la tarjeta por el divisor y compáralo con el dividendo.
Empieza con 5,440 ÷ 16 = 34: multiplica 16 × 34 y compara el producto con 5,440. Ese solo chequeo de tamaño te dice a qué montón va esa puerta.
optional.instructionsEs: Camino 3: Cada puerta muestra una división larga ya terminada. Clasifícalas: ¿la puerta del arcade se enciende como CORRECTA o el cociente está MAL?

optional.label: Path 4: Match each maze door's division problem to the quotient that unlocks it.
optional.explanation: Each door opens with the quotient that rebuilds its dividend: 5,824 ÷ 13 = 448, 9,603 ÷ 11 = 873, 7,912 ÷ 8 = 989, and 6,300 ÷ 25 = 252. Estimating the size helps first — 7,912 ÷ 8 must be close to 1,000, so 989 is the only card that fits.
optional.explanationEs: Cada puerta se abre con el cociente que reconstruye su dividendo: 5,824 ÷ 13 = 448, 9,603 ÷ 11 = 873, 7,912 ÷ 8 = 989 y 6,300 ÷ 25 = 252. Estimar el tamaño ayuda primero: 7,912 ÷ 8 debe estar cerca de 1,000, así que 989 es la única tarjeta que encaja.
hints: Dividing by a smaller divisor leaves a larger quotient, so the sizes of the four answer cards are already a strong clue.
Estimate first, then confirm: round the dividend to a friendly number, divide, and see which card lands in that range.
Try 6,300 ÷ 25: since 25 × 200 = 5,000 and 25 × 300 = 7,500, the quotient sits between 200 and 300. Find the card in that range and multiply back to confirm.
hintsEs: Dividir entre un divisor más pequeño deja un cociente más grande, así que el tamaño de las cuatro tarjetas ya es una pista fuerte.
Estima primero y luego confirma: redondea el dividendo a un número fácil, divide y mira qué tarjeta cae en ese rango.
Prueba 6,300 ÷ 25: como 25 × 200 = 5,000 y 25 × 300 = 7,500, el cociente está entre 200 y 300. Busca la tarjeta en ese rango y multiplica de regreso para confirmar.
optional.labelEs: Camino 4: Une el problema de división de cada puerta del laberinto con el cociente que la abre.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Repair the Arcade Machine

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Repair the machine for 3,724 ÷ 7. Dividend = 3,724, divisor = 7.

workedExample.label: Divide, Multiply, Subtract
workedExample.work: 7 does not fit into 3, so start with 37. 37 ÷ 7 → 5. 5 × 7 = 35, and 37 − 35 = 2

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 2 to make 22. 22 ÷ 7 → 3. 3 × 7 = 21, and 22 − 21 = 1

workedExample.label: Final answer
workedExample.work: Nothing left to bring down. Quotient = 53, remainder = 1

optional.correctWork: The machine quit before the last digit. Look at 3,724 — the final 4 was never brought down. Bring it down next to the 1 to make 14, then run the cycle once more: DIVIDE 14 ÷ 7 → 2, MULTIPLY 2 × 7 = 14, SUBTRACT 14 − 14 = 0. The quotient is 532 with remainder 0, and the check 7 × 532 = 3,724 rebuilds the dividend.
hints: Look at the dividend 3,724. Which of its digits has the machine already used, and which one is still waiting to be brought down?
One digit is still waiting. Bring it down next to the leftover 1, run one more divide–multiply–subtract cycle, then test the result with 7 × quotient.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Repara la máquina de arcade
optional.explanation: The machine stopped before the last digit: after subtracting 21 there was still a 4 in 3,724 waiting to be brought down. Bringing it down makes 14, and 14 ÷ 7 → 2 with 14 − 14 = 0, so the quotient is 532 with remainder 0. The check 7 × 532 = 3,724 rebuilds the dividend instead of the 372 the broken machine reported.
optional.explanationEs: La máquina se detuvo antes del último dígito: después de restar 21 todavía quedaba un 4 en 3,724 esperando bajar. Al bajarlo se forma 14, y 14 ÷ 7 → 2 con 14 − 14 = 0, así que el cociente es 532 con residuo 0. La comprobación 7 × 532 = 3,724 reconstruye el dividendo en vez del 372 que reportó la máquina dañada.

choiceFeedback: 87 reverses the digits of the quotient — and 87 × 12 = 1,044, which is more than 936. Redo the long division and keep each digit in its correct place.
12 × 68 = 816, which lands short of 936. Check the tens digit of your quotient before you bring down the next number.
That is close: 12 × 76 = 912, which is 24 away from 936. Multiply your quotient back by 12 each time to see whether it lands exactly on the dividend.
hints: Estimate first: 12 × 70 = 840 and 12 × 80 = 960, so the quotient must land between 70 and 80.
Set it up as long division and DIVIDE first — how many 12s fit into 93?
DIVIDE: 93 ÷ 12 → 7. MULTIPLY: 7 × 12 = 84. SUBTRACT: 93 − 84 = 9. BRING DOWN the 6 to make 96, then repeat the cycle.
hintsEs: Estima primero: 12 × 70 = 840 y 12 × 80 = 960, así que el cociente debe quedar entre 70 y 80.
Escríbelo como división larga y DIVIDE primero: ¿cuántos 12 caben en 93?
DIVIDE: 93 ÷ 12 → 7. MULTIPLICA: 7 × 12 = 84. RESTA: 93 − 84 = 9. BAJA el 6 para formar 96 y repite el ciclo.

approaching.explanation: 5 × 497 = 2,485. Running the cycle: 24 ÷ 5 → 4 with 4 left, 48 ÷ 5 → 9 with 3 left, 35 ÷ 5 → 7 with 0 left, so the quotient is 497 and the remainder is 0.
choiceFeedback: 487 × 5 = 2,435, which is 50 short of 2,485 — a ten was lost in the middle of the division. Redo it and check each digit as you bring the next one down.
A zero slipped into the tens place: 5 × 507 = 2,535, which is more than 2,485. Recheck what is left after you divide the hundreds.
You are very close, but 5 × 496 = 2,480 and 5 are still left over. A leftover that big means the ones digit is not finished yet.
hints: Size it up: 5 × 500 = 2,500, just a bit more than 2,485 — so the quotient is a little under 500.
Set it up as long division and DIVIDE first — how many 5s fit into 24?
DIVIDE: 24 ÷ 5 → 4. MULTIPLY: 4 × 5 = 20. SUBTRACT: 24 − 20 = 4. BRING DOWN the 8 to make 48, then repeat until the last digit is used.
approaching.explanationEs: 5 × 497 = 2,485. Con el ciclo: 24 ÷ 5 → 4 y sobran 4, 48 ÷ 5 → 9 y sobran 3, 35 ÷ 5 → 7 y sobra 0, así que el cociente es 497 y el residuo es 0.
hintsEs: Mide el tamaño: 5 × 500 = 2,500, apenas más que 2,485, así que el cociente es un poco menor que 500.
Escríbelo como división larga y DIVIDE primero: ¿cuántos 5 caben en 24?
DIVIDE: 24 ÷ 5 → 4. MULTIPLICA: 4 × 5 = 20. RESTA: 24 − 20 = 4. BAJA el 8 para formar 48 y repite hasta usar el último dígito.

approaching.explanation: 9 × 84 = 756. Running the cycle: 75 ÷ 9 → 8 with 3 left, then 36 ÷ 9 → 4 with 0 left, so the quotient is 84 and the remainder is 0.
choiceFeedback: 83 × 9 = 747, which leaves 9 left over — a remainder as big as the divisor means the quotient is too small. Raise the ones digit by one and multiply to check.
9 × 94 = 846, which overshoots 756. Recheck the tens digit by asking how many 9s fit into 75.
9 × 86 = 774, a little past 756. Nudge the ones digit down and multiply back to test it.
hints: Anchor on a fact you know: 9 × 80 = 720, which is close to 756 — so the quotient is just above 80.
Set it up as long division and DIVIDE first — how many 9s fit into 75?
DIVIDE: 75 ÷ 9 → 8. MULTIPLY: 8 × 9 = 72. SUBTRACT: 75 − 72 = 3. BRING DOWN the 6 to make 36, then repeat the cycle.
approaching.explanationEs: 9 × 84 = 756. Con el ciclo: 75 ÷ 9 → 8 y sobran 3, luego 36 ÷ 9 → 4 y sobra 0, así que el cociente es 84 y el residuo es 0.
hintsEs: Apóyate en un dato que ya sabes: 9 × 80 = 720, cerca de 756, así que el cociente está apenas arriba de 80.
Escríbelo como división larga y DIVIDE primero: ¿cuántos 9 caben en 75?
DIVIDE: 75 ÷ 9 → 8. MULTIPLICA: 8 × 9 = 72. RESTA: 75 − 72 = 3. BAJA el 6 para formar 36 y repite el ciclo.

approaching.label: Run the long-division cycle. Fill in the quotient.
hints: Read the row left to right — it is one trip around the cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
The Quotient column wants the WHOLE answer, not just the first digit. Keep repeating the cycle until no digits are left to bring down.
Row 1: after you bring down the 4 you are looking at 64. Divide, multiply and subtract once more, then read the digits you wrote across the top.
approaching.explanation: Long division builds the quotient one digit at a time. In 384 ÷ 8 the first working number is 38: DIVIDE 38 ÷ 8 → 4, MULTIPLY 4 × 8 = 32, SUBTRACT 38 − 32 = 6, BRING DOWN the 4 to make 64, and 64 ÷ 8 → 8 with nothing left — so the quotient is 48. The second row runs the same cycle three times: 6 ÷ 6 → 1, then 7 ÷ 6 → 1 with 1 left, then 12 ÷ 6 → 2, giving 112.
approaching.explanationEs: La división larga construye el cociente un dígito a la vez. En 384 ÷ 8 el primer número de trabajo es 38: DIVIDE 38 ÷ 8 → 4, MULTIPLICA 4 × 8 = 32, RESTA 38 − 32 = 6, BAJA el 4 para formar 64, y 64 ÷ 8 → 8 sin que sobre nada, así que el cociente es 48. La segunda fila repite el mismo ciclo tres veces: 6 ÷ 6 → 1, luego 7 ÷ 6 → 1 y sobra 1, luego 12 ÷ 6 → 2, dando 112.
approaching.labelEs: Repite el ciclo de la división larga. Completa el cociente.
hintsEs: Lee la fila de izquierda a derecha: es una vuelta completa del ciclo divide, multiplica, resta, baja.
La columna Cociente pide la respuesta COMPLETA, no solo el primer dígito. Repite el ciclo hasta que no queden dígitos por bajar.
Fila 1: después de bajar el 4 estás mirando 64. Divide, multiplica y resta una vez más, y luego lee los dígitos que escribiste arriba.

approaching.explanation: 9 × 125 = 1,125. Running the cycle: 11 ÷ 9 → 1 with 2 left, 22 ÷ 9 → 2 with 4 left, 45 ÷ 9 → 5 with 0 left, so the quotient is 125.
choiceFeedback: 115 × 9 = 1,035, not 1,125 — a ten went missing in the middle step. Redo the division: after 9 goes into 11 once, divide the leftover carefully before moving on.
9 × 135 = 1,215, which is past 1,125. Recheck the tens digit by asking how many 9s fit into 22.
So close: 9 × 124 = 1,116, and another 9 still fits. Multiply back every time to see whether you land exactly on the dividend.
hints: Estimate first: 9 × 100 = 900 and 9 × 200 = 1,800, so the quotient lands between 100 and 200.
Set it up as long division and DIVIDE first — how many 9s fit into 11?
DIVIDE: 11 ÷ 9 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 9 = 9. SUBTRACT: 11 − 9 = 2. BRING DOWN the 2 to make 22, then repeat until the last digit is used.
approaching.explanationEs: 9 × 125 = 1,125. Con el ciclo: 11 ÷ 9 → 1 y sobran 2, 22 ÷ 9 → 2 y sobran 4, 45 ÷ 9 → 5 y sobra 0, así que el cociente es 125.

approaching.title: Spot the Mistake in 1,134 ÷ 9

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Divide 1,134 ÷ 9 with long division. Dividend = 1,134, divisor = 9.

workedExample.label: Divide, Multiply, Subtract
workedExample.work: 9 does not fit into 1, so start with 11. 11 ÷ 9 → 1. 1 × 9 = 9, and 11 − 9 = 2

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 3 to make 23. 23 ÷ 9 → 2. 2 × 9 = 18, and 23 − 18 = 5

approaching.correctWork: The student stopped one cycle early: the 4 at the end of 1,134 was never brought down. Bring it down next to the 5 to make 54, then DIVIDE 54 ÷ 9 → 6, MULTIPLY 6 × 9 = 54, SUBTRACT 54 − 54 = 0. The quotient is 126 with remainder 0, and 9 × 126 = 1,134 checks it.
hints: Count the digits of 1,134 that have been used so far. Is one of them still waiting to be brought down?
Bring the last digit down next to the leftover 5, run one more divide–multiply–subtract cycle, then check with 9 × quotient.
approaching.explanation: Every cycle shown is correct, but the work stops too soon: the final 4 of 1,134 was never brought down. Bringing it down makes 54, and 54 ÷ 9 → 6 with 54 − 54 = 0, so the quotient is 126 and the remainder is 0 — confirmed by 9 × 126 = 1,134.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada ciclo mostrado está bien, pero el trabajo se detiene demasiado pronto: el 4 final de 1,134 nunca se bajó. Al bajarlo se forma 54, y 54 ÷ 9 → 6 con 54 − 54 = 0, así que el cociente es 126 y el residuo es 0, confirmado por 9 × 126 = 1,134.

onLevel.label: Complete each division problem.
hints: Every quotient can be checked by multiplying back: quotient × divisor should rebuild the original number exactly.
Run the long-division cycle on every row: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, and repeat until the last digit is used.
For 672 ÷ 8: DIVIDE 67 ÷ 8 → 8, MULTIPLY 8 × 8 = 64, SUBTRACT 67 − 64 = 3, BRING DOWN the 2 to make 32, then repeat. Use the same cycle on every row.
onLevel.explanation: Each quotient comes from repeating divide, multiply, subtract, bring down until the last digit is used: 672 ÷ 8 = 84, 2,208 ÷ 16 = 138, 2,016 ÷ 14 = 144, 1,560 ÷ 15 = 104, and 3,276 ÷ 12 = 273. Multiplying back rebuilds each dividend exactly, so every row ends with a remainder of 0.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada cociente sale de repetir divide, multiplica, resta y baja hasta usar el último dígito: 672 ÷ 8 = 84, 2,208 ÷ 16 = 138, 2,016 ÷ 14 = 144, 1,560 ÷ 15 = 104, y 3,276 ÷ 12 = 273. Al multiplicar de regreso se reconstruye cada dividendo exactamente, así que todas las filas terminan con residuo 0.
hintsEs: Todo cociente se puede comprobar multiplicando al revés: cociente × divisor debe reconstruir exactamente el número original.
Repite el ciclo de la división larga en cada fila: divide, multiplica, resta, baja, y sigue hasta usar el último dígito.
Para 672 ÷ 8: DIVIDE 67 ÷ 8 → 8, MULTIPLICA 8 × 8 = 64, RESTA 67 − 64 = 3, BAJA el 2 para formar 32 y repite. Usa el mismo ciclo en cada fila.

onLevel.label: Match each division problem to its quotient.
hints: Estimation narrows the matches fast: round each dividend and divisor, then see which quotient card is the right size.
You can also work backwards: multiply a quotient card by the divisor and check whether it rebuilds the dividend.
Try 450 ÷ 18: since 18 × 20 = 360 and 18 × 30 = 540, the quotient sits in the twenties. Find the card in that range and verify it.
onLevel.explanation: Every card pairs with the quotient that rebuilds its dividend: 450 ÷ 18 = 25, 1,008 ÷ 16 = 63, 1,440 ÷ 24 = 60, 2,100 ÷ 15 = 140, 864 ÷ 12 = 72, and 1,825 ÷ 25 = 73. Multiplying the quotient by the divisor is the fastest way to confirm a match, since 18 × 25 = 450 and 25 × 73 = 1,825.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta se une con el cociente que reconstruye su dividendo: 450 ÷ 18 = 25, 1,008 ÷ 16 = 63, 1,440 ÷ 24 = 60, 2,100 ÷ 15 = 140, 864 ÷ 12 = 72 y 1,825 ÷ 25 = 73. Multiplicar el cociente por el divisor es la forma más rápida de confirmar una pareja, ya que 18 × 25 = 450 y 25 × 73 = 1,825.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada problema de división con su cociente.
hintsEs: La estimación reduce rápido las opciones: redondea cada dividendo y divisor y mira qué tarjeta de cociente tiene el tamaño correcto.
También puedes trabajar al revés: multiplica una tarjeta de cociente por el divisor y revisa si reconstruye el dividendo.
Prueba 450 ÷ 18: como 18 × 20 = 360 y 18 × 30 = 540, el cociente está en los veintes. Busca la tarjeta en ese rango y compruébala.

onLevel.stem: A warehouse has 2,184 items to pack into boxes of 14. How many boxes are needed?
choiceFeedback: 146 boxes × 14 = 2,044 items, which leaves 140 items unpacked. Multiply your answer by 14 and check that it rebuilds exactly 2,184.
14 × 166 = 2,324, which is more items than the warehouse actually has. Check the tens digit of your quotient.
14 × 155 = 2,170, which leaves 14 items with no box. Multiply back to test whether your quotient uses up every item.
hints: The question asks how many groups of 14 fit into 2,184 — that phrase 'how many boxes' signals division.
Estimate to anchor yourself: 14 × 150 = 2,100 is close to 2,184. Then set it up as long division and run the cycle.
DIVIDE: 21 ÷ 14 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 14 = 14. SUBTRACT: 21 − 14 = 7. BRING DOWN the 8 to make 78, then repeat the cycle.
onLevel.stemEs: Un almacén tiene 2,184 artículos para empacar en cajas de 14. ¿Cuántas cajas se necesitan?
hintsEs: La pregunta es cuántos grupos de 14 caben en 2,184: esa frase 'cuántas cajas' indica división.
Estima para ubicarte: 14 × 150 = 2,100 está cerca de 2,184. Luego escríbelo como división larga y repite el ciclo.
DIVIDE: 21 ÷ 14 → 1. MULTIPLICA: 1 × 14 = 14. RESTA: 21 − 14 = 7. BAJA el 8 para formar 78 y repite el ciclo.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each division problem: does it divide evenly (no remainder), or does it have a remainder?
hints: Each card shows the finished division — scan for the letter 'R', which flags a leftover remainder.
You can also verify a card: multiply quotient × divisor; if it rebuilds the dividend exactly, the division is even.
Check '144 ÷ 12 = 12': 12 × 12 = 144 with nothing left over, so that card goes in Divides Evenly. Verify the others the same way.
onLevel.explanation: A division is even when the quotient times the divisor rebuilds the dividend with nothing left: 12 × 12 = 144, 16 × 30 = 480, and 8 × 125 = 1,000, so those three go under Divides Evenly. The other three show an R because a leftover remains — 7 × 14 = 98 leaves 2, 13 × 38 = 494 leaves 6, and 9 × 27 = 243 leaves 7.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una división es exacta cuando el cociente por el divisor reconstruye el dividendo sin que sobre nada: 12 × 12 = 144, 16 × 30 = 480 y 8 × 125 = 1,000, así que esas tres van en Divide exactamente. Las otras tres muestran una R porque queda un residuo: 7 × 14 = 98 deja 2, 13 × 38 = 494 deja 6 y 9 × 27 = 243 deja 7.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada problema de división: ¿la división es exacta (sin residuo) o tiene residuo?
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta muestra la división terminada: busca la letra 'R', que señala un residuo.
También puedes comprobar una tarjeta: multiplica cociente × divisor; si reconstruye el dividendo exacto, la división es exacta.
Revisa '144 ÷ 12 = 12': 12 × 12 = 144 sin que sobre nada, así que esa tarjeta va en División Exacta. Comprueba las demás igual.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake in 2,058 ÷ 14

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Divide 2,058 ÷ 14 with long division. Dividend = 2,058, divisor = 14.

workedExample.label: Divide, Multiply, Subtract
workedExample.work: 14 does not fit into 2, so start with 20. 20 ÷ 14 → 1. 1 × 14 = 14, and 20 − 14 = 6

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 5 to make 65. 65 ÷ 14 → 4. 4 × 14 = 56, and 65 − 56 = 9

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 8 to make 98. 98 ÷ 14 → 8. 8 × 14 = 112, and 98 − 112 = −14

onLevel.correctWork: The DIVIDE step in the last cycle chose a digit that is too big: 8 × 14 = 112 is more than the 98 you have to subtract from, and you can never subtract more than the working number. The right digit is 7, since 7 × 14 = 98 and 98 − 98 = 0. The quotient is 147 with remainder 0, and 14 × 147 = 2,058 rebuilds the dividend.
hints: Look at the last cycle. After you MULTIPLY, the product has to be small enough to SUBTRACT from 98. Is 112?
A negative difference means the DIVIDE step picked too large a digit. Try the largest digit whose product with 14 still fits inside 98, then finish the cycle.
onLevel.explanation: The last DIVIDE step is where it breaks: the student wrote 8, but 8 × 14 = 112 is larger than the 98 they had to subtract from, so the difference came out negative. The largest digit that fits is 7, since 7 × 14 = 98 leaves 0, so the quotient is 147 and 14 × 147 = 2,058 checks out.
onLevel.explanationEs: El último paso DIVIDE es donde falla: el estudiante escribió 8, pero 8 × 14 = 112 es mayor que los 98 de los que tenía que restar, así que la diferencia salió negativa. El dígito más grande que cabe es 7, ya que 7 × 14 = 98 deja 0, así que el cociente es 147 y 14 × 147 = 2,058 lo comprueba.

extending.title: Find Sonia's Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide
workedExample.work: 16 does not fit into 1 or 15, so start with 153. 153 ÷ 16 → 9, written above the 3

extending.correctWork: The SUBTRACT step is wrong: 153 − 144 = 9, not 19. Long division has a built-in warning here — the difference after you subtract must always be SMALLER than the divisor, and 19 is bigger than 16. With the correct difference of 9, bring down the 6 to make 96, then DIVIDE 96 ÷ 16 → 6 and SUBTRACT 96 − 96 = 0. The quotient is 96 with remainder 0, and 16 × 96 = 1,536.
hints: After you SUBTRACT, compare the difference to the divisor. What should always be true about a difference of 19 when the divisor is 16?
Redo the subtraction 153 − 144 carefully, bring down the 6, and finish the cycle. Then test the result with 16 × quotient.
extending.explanation: Step 3 is the break: 153 − 144 = 9, not 19. Long division has a built-in warning here — if the difference after SUBTRACT is as big as the divisor, another whole group still fits. With the correct difference of 9, bringing down the 6 gives 96, and 96 ÷ 16 → 6 with nothing left, so the quotient is 96 and 16 × 96 = 1,536 confirms it.
extending.explanationEs: El Paso 3 es donde falla: 153 − 144 = 9, no 19. La división larga trae aquí un aviso incorporado: si la diferencia después de RESTAR es tan grande como el divisor, todavía cabe otro grupo entero. Con la diferencia correcta de 9, al bajar el 6 se forma 96, y 96 ÷ 16 → 6 sin que sobre nada, así que el cociente es 96 y 16 × 96 = 1,536 lo confirma.

extending.prompt: The station must load 3,360 ration packs equally into 14 storage pods. Solve it with long division. Name each step — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — and check your answer by multiplying.
extending.sentenceFrame: 3,360 ÷ 14 = ___. I divided ___ by 14 and wrote ___ , then multiplied, subtracted and brought down the next digit each time. I checked by multiplying: 14 × ___ = 3,360.
hints: Re-read the sentence frame: it wants the four named steps — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — not just the answer.
Set it up as 14 ⟌ 3,360. Since 14 does not fit into 3, your first working number is 33.
DIVIDE: 33 ÷ 14 → 2. MULTIPLY: 2 × 14 = 28. SUBTRACT: 33 − 28 = 5. BRING DOWN the 6 to make 56, then repeat — and watch what you must write when you bring down the final 0.
extending.explanation: Long division on 14 ⟌ 3,360 runs the cycle three times: 33 ÷ 14 → 2 (2 × 14 = 28, leaving 5), bring down the 6 → 56 ÷ 14 → 4 (4 × 14 = 56, leaving 0), bring down the 0 → 0 ÷ 14 → 0, so a 0 must be written in the ones place. The quotient is 240 ration packs per pod, and 14 × 240 = 3,360 proves none were left over.
extending.explanationEs: La división larga de 3,360 entre 14 repite el ciclo tres veces: 33 ÷ 14 → 2 (2 × 14 = 28, quedan 5), baja el 6 → 56 ÷ 14 → 4 (4 × 14 = 56, queda 0), baja el 0 → 0 ÷ 14 → 0, así que hay que escribir un 0 en las unidades. El cociente es 240 paquetes de raciones por cápsula, y 14 × 240 = 3,360 comprueba que no sobró ninguno.
extending.promptEs: La estación debe cargar 3,360 paquetes de raciones por partes iguales en 14 cápsulas de almacenamiento. Resuélvelo con división larga. Nombra cada paso — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — y comprueba tu respuesta multiplicando.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer el modelo de oración: pide los cuatro pasos con su nombre — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — no solo la respuesta.
Escríbelo como 14 ⟌ 3,360. Como 14 no cabe en 3, tu primer número de trabajo es 33.
DIVIDE: 33 ÷ 14 → 2. MULTIPLICA: 2 × 14 = 28. RESTA: 33 − 28 = 5. BAJA el 6 para formar 56 y repite; fíjate en lo que debes escribir al bajar el último 0.

extending.label: Solve each problem using long division. Show the quotient and any remainder.
hints: Each row asks for TWO things: the whole-number quotient AND whatever is left over — and a remainder can be 0.
Run the long-division cycle — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — until no digits remain; the last leftover is the remainder.
For 2,578 ÷ 13: begin with 25 ÷ 13 → 1, subtract 13, bring down the 7. Keep cycling and record whatever remains at the very end.
extending.explanation: Long division keeps going until no digits are left to bring down, and whatever is still there is the remainder: 2,578 ÷ 13 gives 198 R 4, 3,456 ÷ 16 gives 216 R 0, and 1,987 ÷ 11 gives 180 R 7. You can check each row with divisor × quotient + remainder, since 13 × 198 + 4 = 2,578 and 11 × 180 + 7 = 1,987.
extending.explanationEs: La división larga continúa hasta que no queden dígitos por bajar, y lo que todavía esté ahí es el residuo: 2,578 ÷ 13 da 198 R 4, 3,456 ÷ 16 da 216 R 0 y 1,987 ÷ 11 da 180 R 7. Puedes comprobar cada fila con divisor × cociente + residuo, ya que 13 × 198 + 4 = 2,578 y 11 × 180 + 7 = 1,987.
extending.labelEs: Resuelve cada problema con división larga. Escribe el cociente y el residuo, si lo hay.
hintsEs: Cada fila pide DOS cosas: el cociente entero Y lo que sobra, y un residuo puede ser 0.
Repite el ciclo de la división larga — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — hasta que no queden dígitos; lo último que sobra es el residuo.
Para 2,578 ÷ 13: empieza con 25 ÷ 13 → 1, resta 13 y baja el 7. Sigue el ciclo y anota lo que quede al final.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Multi-Digit Numbers is skipping a placeholder zero in the quotient when a digit doesn't divide evenly, which shifts every digit after it out of place. For example, dividing 3,216 ÷ 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1, but the next digit 2 doesn't divide by 3, so a 0 must be written before continuing — bring down the 1 to make 21 ÷ 3 = 7, then bring down 6 ÷ 3 = 2, giving the correct quotient 1,072. A student who skips writing that 0 and jumps straight to 21 ÷ 3 = 7 ends up with 172 instead of 1,072 — an answer off by a factor of ten. Always check: does a digit in your quotient go missing every time you 'can't divide'? If so, you dropped a placeholder zero.

connect.scenario: A school is ordering 1,680 pencils to distribute equally to 24 classrooms for the school year.
connect.promptQuestion: How does multi-digit division help the school figure out how many pencils each classroom gets?

check.stem: Estimate first: rounding to 1,600 ÷ 20 gives about how many pencils per room?
check.explanation: 1,600 ÷ 20 = 80, so the exact answer should land near 80. Getting 70 is reasonable; getting 7 or 700 would signal a place-value slip.

check.stem: If the pencils were split among 20 classrooms instead of 24, would each room get more or fewer?
choices: More, because the pencils are split among fewer rooms
The same, because the total did not change
check.explanation: 1,680 ÷ 20 = 84. Splitting the same total among fewer rooms gives each room more.

connect.modelAnswer: 1,680 ÷ 24 = 70, so each classroom gets 70 pencils. Check by multiplying back: 24 × 70 = 1,680.

exitTicket.explanation: 16 × 147 = 2,352. Running the cycle: 23 ÷ 16 → 1 with 7 left, 75 ÷ 16 → 4 with 11 left, 112 ÷ 16 → 7 with 0 left, so the quotient is 147 with no remainder.
exitTicket.hint: Think through the problem step by step.
choiceFeedback: Re-multiply your answer by 16; does it return to 2,352?
Close — check the remainder and the ones place of your quotient.
hints: Size it up first: 16 × 100 = 1,600 and 16 × 200 = 3,200, so the quotient lands somewhere between 100 and 200.
Set it up as 16 ⟌ 2,352 and run the cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
DIVIDE: 23 ÷ 16 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 16 = 16. SUBTRACT: 23 − 16 = 7. BRING DOWN the 5 to make 75, then repeat until the last digit is used.
